items.title: MissingMethodException after patching any method with a call to built-in Unity method
items.body:
**Describe the bug**
Patching any method containing a call to Unity built-in functions (such as GameObject.Find or Random.Range) results in a MissingMethodException on an attempt to call this built-in function from ANY other method!

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. The original method and its signature and class
```
  private Room CreateNewLargeRoom()
  {
    Room room = new Room();
    if (this.InternalMapInfo.SpawnRoom == null)
    {
      room.xDimention = this.SpawnRoomSize;
      room.zDimention = this.SpawnRoomSize;
    }
    else
    {
      room.xDimention = Random.Range(this.MinRoomSize, this.MaxRoomSize + 1);
      room.zDimention = Random.Range(this.MinRoomSize, this.MaxRoomSize + 1);
    }
    return room;
  }
```

2. The patch code
```
    [HarmonyPatch(typeof(MapGenerator))]
    [HarmonyPatch("CreateNewLargeRoom")]
    class PatchTestTranspile
    {
        static IEnumerable<CodeInstruction> Transpiler(IEnumerable<CodeInstruction> instructions)
        {
            foreach (var instr in instructions) yield return instr;
        }
    }
```

4. The stacktrace or other errors
```
MissingMethodException: Attempted to access a missing method.
  at (wrapper managed-to-native) UnityEngine.Random.RandomRangeInt(int,int)
```

```
  at (wrapper managed-to-native) UnityEngine.Random.RandomRangeInt(int,int)
```

As you see those are 2 different **unpatched** methods that now produce an exception.

**Expected behavior**
Built-in Unity method calls should not produce the aforementioned exception.

**Screenshots / Code**
-

**Runtime environment (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: Windows 10, 64bit
 - .NET version: 4.8
 - Harmony version 2.0.4
- Name of game or host application: COMPOUND (Unity 2019.3.10)

**Additional context**
Have anyone tested this lib with more recent versions of Unity? It seems to me there might be some incompatibility issue.
